original_question: Let h(X) = X^3 - 3X + 1, let alpha be a root of h, let alpha' = alpha^2 - 2, and let K = Q(alpha). With respect to the integral basis {1, alpha, alpha'}, the norm form is T(a, b, c) = N(a + b alpha + c alpha') = a^3 - b^3 - c^3 - 3ab^2 - 3ac^2 + 3abc + 6b^2c - 3bc^2. Determine all functions f, h: Z -> C such that T(f(a), f(b), f(c)) = h(T(a, b, c)).
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 7 of arXiv:1609.09842, i.e. the explicit cubic-field special case of Problem 6 on pseudo-automorphisms of norm forms. In the cited source paper [2], this is the Problem 2 side of the theory (the condition that the transformed norm form depend only on the original norm-form value), not the distinct Problem 1 equation f(T)=T(f).
correct_elements: The draft already captures the right special case: the cubic field K=Q(alpha) attached to X^3-3X+1, the integral basis {1, alpha, alpha'}, the explicit norm form T(a,b,c)=N_{K/Q}(a+b alpha+c alpha'), and the intended classification problem in which T(f(a),f(b),f(c)) is controlled only by T(a,b,c) via an auxiliary function h. This is very close to the paper’s singled-out Problem 7 and does not broaden beyond the paper.
missing_details: It should say explicitly that the functional equation is required for all integers a,b,c.
The polynomial and the auxiliary function should not both be called h; a stand-alone statement should rename one of them to avoid ambiguity.
It should clarify that alpha' = alpha^2 - 2 is another root (a Galois conjugate) of X^3 - 3X + 1.
It should state that {1, alpha, alpha'} is an integral basis of the ring of integers O_K of K.
It should make explicit that T is the field norm N_{K/Q}, so T maps Z^3 into Z.
To match the paper-faithful formulation, it should note that the real content is that T(f(a),f(b),f(c)) depends only on T(a,b,c); introducing an auxiliary h is just a coding of that dependence.
Strictly, the auxiliary output function only needs to be defined on the value set T(Z^3); if one writes h: Z -> C, that means one is choosing an arbitrary extension off that set.
It should say that no regularity, continuity, multiplicativity, or growth assumptions are imposed on f or h beyond being functions on Z.

It should distinguish this Problem 2 / pseudo-automorphism question from the different Problem 1 equation f(T(a,b,c)) = T(f(a),f(b),f(c)), whose h=f special case is the one treated in the cited 2005 paper.
refined_question: Let p(X) = X^3 - 3X + 1, let alpha be a root of p, and put alpha' = alpha^2 - 2. Then K = Q(alpha) is the cubic field generated by alpha, {1, alpha, alpha'} is an integral basis of O_K, and the associated norm form is T(a,b,c) = N_{K/Q}(a + b alpha + c alpha') = a^3 - b^3 - c^3 - 3ab^2 - 3ac^2 + 3abc + 6b^2c - 3bc^2 for integers a,b,c. Classify all pairs of functions f: Z -> C and H: T(Z^3) -> C such that T(f(a), f(b), f(c)) = H(T(a,b,c)) for every a,b,c in Z.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, determine all functions f: Z -> C such that T(f(a), f(b), f(c)) depends only on the value of T(a,b,c) for all a,b,c in Z.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s special cubic problem, not a neighboring broader or different problem. In arXiv:1609.09842, Section 4 first states the general pseudo-automorphism problem for norm forms (Problem 6) and then isolates the cubic field defined by X^3-3X+1 as Problem 7. The underlying conceptual formulation comes from the cited 2005 paper’s Problem 2, which asks for those f for which the transformed norm form depends only on the original norm-form value. Section 5 of that 2005 paper supplies exactly the same cubic field, integral basis {1, alpha, alpha'}, and explicit norm form T. By contrast, Proposition 3 there solves the different Problem 1 equation f(T)=T(f) for this cubic field; that is why the note remarks only on the already-solved h=f special case, and why the refined question should remain the open Problem 7 classification rather than being replaced by Proposition 3.
